title: Sonnet II
text:
Who does not weep for what is past,

seeing how the present goes?

Who is

        the one who does not feel

what fortune has taken away?

I

        once saw myself well loved,

my desire on a high summit;

to contemplate the

        past-

memory wounds me.

And

        since everything is absent from me,

I do not know which remedy to choose;

good and evil alike

        anger me,

poor wretch who feels it!

        There was a time, and proud hours,

which my life enjoyed,

where sorrowfully

        were sown

the seeds of my gray hairs.

And

        since, if he holds it good,

I can well speak this way.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the fragmentary indentation and the unfinished, archaic turn of Castillejo's lament.

title: That
text:
We were riding through the fields

    in a wagon at dawn.

    A red rose wound in the darkness.



    And suddenly a hare crossed the road.

    One of us pointed to it with his hand.

    That was long ago. Today none of them is alive,

    neither the hare, nor the man who made the gesture.



    Oh, my love, where are they, where have they gone?

    The flash of a hand, the line of a movement,

    the whisper of pebbles.

    I ask not with sadness, but with wonder.




Version by Rafael

        Díaz Borbón
editorial_note: The translation follows the supplied Spanish version and preserves the translator credit in the source text.
